predecessors.name: Later Liang
predecessors.text: Lianchuan, Xiping and Ledu on the Huangshui, the Southern Liang's own land (the page's last 'few commanderies along the Huangshui River')

successors.name: Western Qin
successors.text: Lianchuan, Xiping and Ledu on the Huangshui, the Southern Liang's own land (the page's last 'few commanderies along the Huangshui River')

ledger.x: 397: Tufa Wugu proclaims the Southern Liang at Xiping.
399: Lilugu succeeds Wugu, claims the title Prince of Hexi and moves the capital to Xiping.
402: Rutan succeeds Lilugu, claims the title King of Liang and moves the capital back to Ledu.
410: Guzang falls to the Northern Liang.
414: the Western Qin takes Ledu and the Southern Liang ends.

wars.name: Southern Liang-Later Liang wars
wars.outcome: Lilugu defeated the Later Liang twice and allied with the Northern Liang; no land is named and the Later Liang gave its remnant to Later Qin in 403.

wars.name: Later Qin siege of Guzang
wars.outcome: Later Qin besieged Guzang, a revolt broke out inside the city, Rutan repelled the attack and made peace and re-declared himself King of Liang.

wars.name: Southern Liang-Northern Liang war
wars.outcome: Rutan invaded the Northern Liang in 407 and was routed (the page adds that Helian Xia defeated him in the Ordos that year); several failed campaigns 408-410; Guzang fell to the Northern Liang in 410.

wars.name: Western Qin conquest of Southern Liang
wars.outcome: The Western Qin captured Ledu and the rest surrendered; the Tuyuhun and the Western Qin had both attacked the state earlier (undated).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line; the Huangshui frontier and the Guzang holding of 406-410 are approximate, and the page names no commanderies.
